scenario.name: Google Cloud Security, Wiz & MITRE — GCP Cloud Build Default Service Account & Artifact Registry Audit
scenario.overview: Picture an active industrial factory floor with a moving assembly conveyor belt, an articulated yellow robotic arm, steel parts bins, and a final quality-seal stamping desk. During the quiet night shift on the factory floor, a saboteur steps beside the moving assembly conveyor right before the automated quality stamp. In this real-world scenario, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the factory quality stamp station in tiny disguised batches, then smuggles copied records out past the factory quality stamp station in tiny disguised batches. Only when a quality engineer checks the finished product’s weight and internal wiring against the locked master blueprint cabinet does the factory-line swap appear. In this scenario (T1648, Google Cloud Security, Wiz & MITRE, GCP Cloud Build Default Service Account & Artifact Registry Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: submitting Ad-Hoc Cloud Build Job, then worker Container Metadata Query, then artifact Registry. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Submitting Ad-Hoc Cloud Build Job, then Worker Container Metadata Query, then Artifact Registry, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates process, authentication, and network telemetry for T1648 across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Submitting Ad-Hoc Cloud Build Job via google.devtools.cloudbuild.v1.CloudBuild.CreateBuild
stages.subtitle: Execution (T1648 - Serverless Execution)
stages.description: During the quiet night shift on the factory floor, a saboteur steps beside the moving assembly conveyor right before the automated quality stamp. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the factory quality stamp station in tiny disguised batches while everyday visitors and the factory quality inspector go about their routine. A compromised identity holding roles/cloudbuild.builds.editor (or cloudbuild.builds.create) submits an inline cloudbuild.yaml build step via gcloud builds submit, recorded in GCP Admin Activity Cloud Audit Logs (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with GcpService=cloudbuild.googleapis.com, MethodName=google.devtools.cloudbuild.v1.CloudBuild.CreateBuild, CallerPrincipal=dev-ci-user@corp-prod-01.iam.gserviceaccount.com so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.methodName="google.devtools.cloudbuild.v1.CloudBuild.CreateBuild"' --limit=10 (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.methodName="google.devtools.cloudbuild.v1.CloudBuild.Create so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1648 during "Submitting Ad-Hoc Cloud Build Job via google.devtools.cloudbuild.v1.CloudBuild.CreateBuild" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). Next, the follow-up artifact gcloud builds describe <build-id> runs (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , gcloud builds describe <build-id> against AWS CloudTrail, GCP Cloud Audit, or Microsoft Entra so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1648 during "Submitting Ad-Hoc Cloud Build Job via google.devtools.cloudbuild.v1.CloudBuild.CreateBuild" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ google.devtools.cloudbuild.v1.CloudBuild.CreateBuild / ⇠#1 ACK 200) from Node ① (#1 Developer Role (cloudbuild.builds.create)) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Artifact Registry & GCS Storage Buckets).

keySpecs.value: Disable the legacy default Cloud Build Service Account privilege assignment via Organization Policy constraints/cloudbuild.useBuildServiceAccount and require user-specified least-privilege service accounts per build trigger.

stages.title: Stage 2: Worker Container Metadata Query for @cloudbuild.gserviceaccount.com OAuth2 Token
stages.subtitle: Privilege Escalation (T1552.005 - Cloud Instance Metadata API)
stages.description: The robotic arm pauses for a heartbeat as the saboteur swaps one genuine component on the belt for an identical-looking counterfeit part carrying a hidden wire. Here in Step 2 inside the factory floor, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the factory quality inspector's station without disturbing the original master blueprint cabinet. Inside the Cloud Build step container, the build command queries http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/token (with header Metadata-Flavor: Google) to retrieve the OAuth2 access token of <project-number>@cloudbuild.gserviceaccount.com (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with MetadataEndpoint=http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/token, InheritedIdentity=445566778899@cloudbuild.gserviceaccount.com, BuildStepImage=gcr.io/cloud-builders/gcloud so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes gcloud projects get-iam-policy corp-prod-01 --flatten="bindings[].members" --filter="bindings.members:cloudbuild.gserviceaccount.com" (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , gcloud projects get-iam-policy corp-prod-01 --flatten="bindings[].members" --filter="bindings so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1552.005 during "Worker Container Metadata Query for @cloudbuild.gserviceaccount.com OAuth2 Token" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). Next, the follow-up artifact gcloud logging read 'resource.type="build"' --limit=20 runs (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , gcloud logging read 'resource.type="build"' --limit=20 against AWS CloudTrail, GCP Cloud Audi so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1552.005 during "Worker Container Metadata Query for @cloudbuild.gserviceaccount.com OAuth2 Token" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ curl -H "Metadata-Flavor: Google" http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/token / ⇠#2 ACK 200) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 GCP Cloud Build API (builds.create)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Artifact Registry & GCS Storage Buckets).

keySpecs.value: Remove broad roles/editor or roles/cloudbuild.builds.builder permissions from the default <project-number>@cloudbuild.gserviceaccount.com identity and enforce VPC Service Controls around Cloud Build worker pools.

stages.title: Stage 3: Artifact Registry & Cloud Storage Source Archive Access Audit
stages.subtitle: Collection (T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage)
stages.description: The assembly line rolls forward, the factory press stamps the official warranty seal right onto the tampered unit, and trucks ship it to every trusting customer. In this final step inside the factory floor, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the factory quality stamp station in tiny disguised batches until the assembly line inspection camera catches the mismatch. Using the Cloud Build service account token, the actor reads container images in Artifact Registry and staging archives in gs://<project>_cloudbuild/source/, logged in GCP Data Access Audit Logs (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with AuditLogStream=cloudaudit.googleapis.com/data_access, MethodName=storage.objects.get, TargetBucketObject=gs://corp-prod-01_cloudbuild/source/1763312400.tgz so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail="445566778899@cloudbuild.gserviceaccount.com" AND logName:"cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Fdata_access"' (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail="445566778899@cloudbuild. so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1530 during "Artifact Registry & Cloud Storage Source Archive Access Audit" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). Next, the follow-up artifact gcloud iam service-accounts disable 445566778899@cloudbuild.gserviceaccount.com runs (which executes a cloud control-plane API or CLI operation , gcloud iam service-accounts disable 445566778899@cloudbuild.gserviceaccount.com against AWS C so that harvests cloud identity tokens, escalates IAM privileges, or exfiltrates cloud data , T1530 during "Artifact Registry & Cloud Storage Source Archive Access Audit" without deploying traditional endpoint malware, captured in CloudTrail / Unified Audit Log telemetry). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ storage.objects.get on buckets/corp-prod-01_cloudbuild/objects/source/archive.tgz / ⇠#3 ACK 200) from Node ③ (#3 GCP Cloud Build API (builds.create)) to Node ④ (#4 Cloud Build Worker Metadata Server), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Artifact Registry & GCS Storage Buckets).

keySpecs.value: Enable GCP Data Access Audit Logs (DATA_READ / DATA_WRITE) for Cloud Storage and Artifact Registry and monitor Security Command Center (SCC) for anomalous Cloud Build Service Account calls from outside Google IP space.
